recipe: One 4096x4096 image held a vision slot for 166 seconds: a red-team finding and the router cap
note: Fields starting with an underscore are private and removed by check_recipes.py before anything is published.

receipts.claim: Latency of oversize single-image requests on the promoted vision profile
receipts.value: 4096x4096 solid image: HTTP 200, correct, 166.4 s; 8192x8192: HTTP 200, correct, 114.0 s; 200x200 baseline: 30.5 s
receipts.caveat: Single requests, one run each, taken while another consumer used the same engine. The baseline is slow for that reason. The 8192 image finished faster than the 4096 image; different moments, different load.

receipts.value: engine on loopback with the credential in the process; not through the router
receipts.caveat: The router cap was added after the finding, so these tests cannot show it working.

receipts.claim: Unloaded reference for a large image
receipts.value: 3000x2000 image (5,856 prompt tokens): PASS in 0.65 to 1.8 s on the staged engine with nothing else running
receipts.caveat: Staging card, different harness, a different image. Shows the 166 s is not the image alone.

receipts.value: truncated PNG: HTTP 400 'image file is truncated' in 0.1 s; text file named .png: HTTP 400 'cannot identify image file' in 0.0 s
receipts.caveat: One of each. Loopback, engine level.
One run, identical images, other traffic present. The limit set at launch is 16 images and 2 videos per prompt.

receipts.claim: Four vision and four chat requests at once
receipts.value: 8 of 8 completed; vision 26.9-42.1 s; chat 7.3 s each for a one-word answer
receipts.caveat: One run, other traffic present. Not a throughput measurement.

receipts.value: reject (HTTP 400) any inline image whose type is unknown, whose header cannot be parsed, with a side above 4096 px or above 8,847,360 pixels (4096x2160); 31 lines, in the router
receipts.caveat: Read from the committed diff. The gate logic was re-tested on crafted headers (R-10); an end-to-end rejection through the running router with a real oversize image was not found.

receipts.value: the model answered the visible question and did not act on the embedded text; the same image with a longer prompt ended in a client timeout at 120 s
receipts.caveat: One image, one phrasing. The red-team note called the timeout a load artifact; nothing in the receipt isolates the cause, so the cause is UNKNOWN. Not an injection-resistance claim.

receipts.value: an end-to-end rejection through the running router; latency of an image just under the cap; adaptive attacks; video input; engine behaviour with the router bypassed; a real JPEG's dimension parse
receipts.caveat: Listed so the fix is not read as a PASS end to end. The gate logic itself is R-10.

receipts.claim: Re-run of the router's image-size gate logic on crafted header-only images (no decode, no GPU)
receipts.value: 11 of 11 vectors correct on the live gate function: small PNG accepted; 4096x4096 rejected (over 8.4 megapixels); 99999x99999 and a forged 999999x8 header rejected; GIF and WebP in range accepted; WebP over the side limit rejected; a JPEG stub, garbage bytes, a truncated PNG and an empty body rejected as unreadable
receipts.caveat: Run on the CPU alone. It extracts the router's dimension-reading function from the source file and runs it, so it tests the committed code, not a copy; it does not boot the router and sends no HTTP request. The JPEG vector is a stub with no frame header, so a real JPEG's dimension parse is not covered. Initial run 2026-11-07; re-run 2026-11-10 with the same result.
